setupSteps: Pick the version. *Standing, back near a wall:* feet hip-width, knees soft, shoulder blades about a hand's width from the wall so a swing would touch it. *Seated:* a firm upright chair or bench with back support, feet flat, sit tall. Sources say the seat and back support make it harder to swing with the legs, hips or lower back (Centr, Tonal, snippets). *No equipment:* bottles, rucksack or towel in the same positions.
Floor. Non-slip mat on a flat spot; a folded towel beside you to set the weights on.
Pick up the dumbbells safely. Bend knees and hips, keep the back flat, lift them to your sides. Do not rock them up with your back.
Starting position. Arms hanging beside the body, elbows pressed lightly against the ribs, elbow nearly straight (a very slight bend, not locked).

Grip. *Hammer (recommended first):* palms facing the thighs, thumbs pointing forward. *Supinated bicep curl:* palms start facing forward or turn up as the weight rises. Hold firmly with thumbs wrapped. *Wrists:* straight in line with the forearm, not bent back (several sources, snippets).
Brace. Ribs down, glutes lightly tight, tummy tight, shoulders down and slightly back, chin level.
Choose the weight. The lightest weight that lets you do 10 slow reps with 3-4 in the tank (section 7).
Camera. Phone in landscape at about hip-to-chest height (100-120 cm, est.), 2-2.5 m away, filming the side of the curling arm.
Warm up 3-5 minutes (est.): march on the spot, arm circles, shoulder rolls, wrist circles, and one set of 8 reps with very light weights or empty hands.

steps.title: Stand tall with the weights at your sides
steps.action: Stand with your back near the wall, dumbbells hanging at your sides, thumbs forward.
steps.feel: Weight in both hands, whole foot on the floor.
steps.visualCheck: Side: ear, shoulder and hip in a line; arm nearly straight. Front: shoulders level.

steps.title: Pin the elbows
steps.action: Press the upper arms lightly against your ribs and brace.
steps.feel: Elbows tucked beside the torso, shoulders down.
steps.visualCheck: Side: the elbow sits beside the hip line.

steps.title: Curl up
steps.action: Bend the elbow and lift the dumbbell toward the shoulder; the upper arm stays still. For the supinated curl, turn the palm up as it rises.
steps.feel: The front of the upper arm and forearm working; no push from the shoulder.
steps.visualCheck: Side: only the forearm moves; the elbow does not drift forward; the body does not lean back.

steps.title: Squeeze at the top
steps.action: Stop when the dumbbell is near the shoulder, without shrugging the shoulder up.
steps.feel: A tight front of the arm.
steps.visualCheck: Side: elbow angle about 30-60 degrees (est.); the wrist is straight.

steps.title: Lower slowly
steps.action: Straighten the elbow back toward the starting position in a controlled way.
steps.feel: The arm lengthening under control, no dropping.
steps.visualCheck: Side: the same path down; the elbow stays pinned; the body stays tall.

steps.title: Reach the bottom with a nearly straight arm
steps.action: Let the arm get nearly straight (soft elbow) before the next rep. Do not bounce.
steps.feel: A small pause with the weight hanging.
steps.visualCheck: Side: elbow angle at or above about 150 degrees (est.).

steps.title: Repeat for 8-12 reps, then alternate if wanted
steps.action: Curl both arms together, or one at a time, the resting arm staying at the side (ACE hammer-curl entry, snippet).
steps.breathing: Out on the curl, in on the lowering.
steps.visualCheck: Both arms follow the same path and range.

steps.title: Set the dumbbells down safely
steps.action: Bend the knees and hips with a flat back and set the dumbbells on the mat or towel with a 2-3 s count.
steps.visualCheck: Side: back flat; the only sound is a soft touch.

commonMistakes.title: Swinging the body (the "cheat curl")
commonMistakes.text: Swinging the body (the "cheat curl"). Why: shifts the work to the hips, shoulders and lower back, takes tension off the arm (Livestrong, Peloton, snippets). Fix: lighter weight, back near a wall or seated, 3 s lowering.

commonMistakes.title: Elbows drifting forward or flaring out
commonMistakes.text: Elbows drifting forward or flaring out. Why: brings the front shoulder in and reduces the arm work (Livestrong and others, snippets). Fix: elbows lightly on the ribs; if you cannot keep them, go lighter.

commonMistakes.title: Shrugging at the top
commonMistakes.text: Shrugging at the top. Why: the neck and upper trapezius take over. Fix: shoulders down, stop when the weight is near the shoulder.

commonMistakes.title: Partial range of motion
commonMistakes.text: Partial range of motion. Why: sources say a short range cuts the benefit and often comes from too heavy a weight (Livestrong, snippets). Fix: nearly straight arm at the bottom, weight near the shoulder at the top, same range each rep.

commonMistakes.title: Dropping the weight fast (no controlled lowering)
commonMistakes.text: Dropping the weight fast (no controlled lowering). Why: loses half the work and jerks the elbow tendon; a rehab source calls the lowering phase of a heavy curl the main stress after a distal biceps tendon repair (snippet). Fix: 3 s down.

commonMistakes.title: Bending the wrist
commonMistakes.text: Bending the wrist. Why: loads the wrist and forearm tendons. Fix: wrist straight and in line, grip firm, lighter weight.

commonMistakes.title: Weight too heavy
commonMistakes.text: Weight too heavy. Why: causes all of the above. Fix: choose by 3-4 reps in reserve (section 7).

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath. Why: raises blood pressure and brings dizziness (PubMed 7741618, carried). Fix: out on the curl, in on the lowering.

commonMistakes.title: Dropping dumbbells on the floor
commonMistakes.text: Dropping dumbbells on the floor. Why: noise for neighbours below and risk to feet. Fix: lower with a 2-3 s count onto a mat.

commonMistakes.title: Locking the elbow hard at the bottom and bouncing
commonMistakes.text: Locking the elbow hard at the bottom and bouncing. Why: jolts the elbow. Fix: soft elbow, a short pause.

safetyNotes: Elbow and wrist tendon pain (tennis or golfer's elbow, tendinopathy): gripping and forearm rotation can aggravate symptoms (RACGP HANDI and AAFP lateral epicondylitis pages, snippets). NHS-type tennis elbow booklets use light neutral-grip weight work at the elbow in rehab (snippet), so the hammer grip may suit some people, but a trial of curls for tennis elbow: Not found. Start very light, stop if pain climbs, and ask a physiotherapist.

Biceps tendon problems: after a distal biceps tendon repair, heavy eccentric curls are avoided for months (physio-pedia and a rehab source, snippets); ask the surgical team. A sudden pop, bruising or a bulge in the upper arm means stop and get medical attention (Cleveland Clinic page, snippet).
Shoulder problems: the front shoulder is loaded when the elbow drifts forward; stop if the front of the shoulder hurts and keep the elbows pinned. A clinical source for curls specifically: Not found.
Lower back problems: use the seated version or stand with the back near a wall, no leaning; ACE warns that swinging the torso back in a seated machine curl stresses the low back (snippet).
High blood pressure and heart disease: breathe out on the curl, never hold the breath, light weight; get clearance first with heart disease or uncontrolled blood pressure.
Osteoporosis: loaded strength work is generally recommended; the curl itself is low risk for the spine if the trunk stays still; with a vertebral fracture or severe osteoporosis ask a clinician.

Pregnancy and postpartum: a light seated curl is generally treated as low risk in uncomplicated pregnancy (PMC11193983 resistance training in pregnancy, carried; snippet), but ask your obstetrician, midwife or women's health physiotherapist; stop with dizziness, headache, pain, leaking or pelvic heaviness. ACOG's own wording: Not found.
Mumbai flat: mat under your feet, set the dumbbells down gently, no glass bottles, keep clear of furniture and the balcony, and no swinging a rucksack near people or windows.
